If you are rerolling your account and find yourself finding heroes with "Yes / Definitely / Absolutely", you can consider keeping it. Just be aware that keeping colo/buff oriented hero can make progressing through challenge mode difficult if you don't have a good PvE Hero.
Useful for unlocking an essential warrior skill, SoV. Practically useless outside of it.
Have you ever seen a nuclear bomb? This thing is about as powerful and unethical as that. The buffpocalypse has arrived, and there is no way to avoid it.
Extremely powerful in colosseum, since he provides a net 80% eva. The entire Eva meta is defined by him.
It's best to think of her flag as a literal immortality field. Well, if you are in it at least.
Often used as trigger for Fireaxe for 3 chain auto team. Self damage potential isn't bad either post-buff.
A ridiculous neutral damage dealer that comes with very consistent damage outputs. Though, knockbacks and stuns are still issues for her.
Beginning of another age of powercreep due to his incredible dmg potential, but has since lost favor due to accessibility and power of promo options.
The single least investment required option to clear PvE. However, you are bound to come across options that will perform better given more investment.
A very annoying hero to deal with in arena, especially when paired with a second DPS. Consider picking him if you want to enlarge your arena choices.
A solid pick in arena with two types of playstyle depending on how you use him; a solid choice in arena given his crowd control capabilities.
Ridiculous damage potential with massive self atk buffs, but is incredibly block hungry, like usual. Picking buffers for her can be a little annoying though.
The cheat code of Total War, your one stop shop to farming accessories, clears Hard and Nightmare with promotable support in her team and 9 dead bodies (useless in Inferno)
Useful for unlocking an essential Paladin skill, SoP. Practically useless outside of it.
Useful for unlocking lv 3 and 4 upgrades of a strong Paladin skill, ToV. Strong choice in colo as well, however is hard countered by debuff immunity.
Hits per lance is dependent upon self and ally size, and increases further if enemy is off-screen. Possesses quite scary one-shot capabilities in arena.
Offers a lot of role consolidation as a tank, bringing shred and buff prevention to the table alongside self eva buff, and doubling of her Armor/Resis.
The best general tank in game, with self DR, Armor, Resis buff, and CR aura, and can consistently put up tanking. When up against tank ignores however...
Can be used with Shasha for 3 chain auto team.
The best physical tank in-game due to his stacking DR and massive self Armor buffs, along with a lot, a LOT of stuns.
Possesses a very unique kit with magical damage amp as well as undispellable tanking. Niche, but may be irreplacable at times.
Strong choice for PvE if you have Resu skill. Keep him at low inheritance levels in early game to allow him to set up more easily.
Luci, less tanky, but much more utility for magical DPSes. Although tanking can be dispelled it is immediately reapplied upon ally 3 chain.
Wall personified, except she also has interesting damage potential when given high heal count like Bari with Sanctuary when it comes to Ibelin abuse. A good pick in general.
Strong albeit inconsistent auto buff on top of ridiculous shielding capabilities makes her an absolute monster in arena. Weak to dispel though.
Fast and consistent damage output with excellent damage mechanics. Though her slow pace of gaining SP can be problematic especially in PvE.
Useful for unlocking an overpowered archer skill, RFS. Practically useless outside of it.
High damage, consistent knockups, and practically inifinite range. Incredibly good both as a support and as a DPS for the latest raid.
A chase 3 hero with competent burst, but only shines in raid settings due to targeting issues. Pair with Jeomrye to bring out her full potential.
Infinite range, good hit count, and good damage allows her to acquire good clear times in end game challenge.
Melee archer with very good damage capability alongside self pen buff. Can be useful when contents restricting ranged heroes is relevant.
Useful for unlocking an overpowered hunter skill, DS. Practically useless outside of it.
Consistent and ridiculous burst potential. This alongside no bullet travel time makes her one of the best DPSes in PvE as of now. However, this is just the start.
One of the most frequently used sub DPS in ordeal thanks to her ridiculous 3 chain frequency, alongside good damage and buffs. She flies too.
Frequent dispel alongside buff prevention and shred is not something to be taken lightly.
A very generic DPS but also hits very very hard, alongside good hit count. But most importantly of all, cat girls are irresistable.
Does a bit of everything for Total War, albeit not as good as Schild. Considering she's consistent in applying debuff, her utility outmatches most other choices there.
Useful for unlocking an essential wizard skill, SM. Practically useless outside of it.
High hit count scarecrows with consistent damage output, either by herself or with Ibelin abuse. Try her if you have her and SM.
Damage is the very definition of insanity, and have forced devs to design contents to restrict her in particular. Mostly locked with Lia.
Rabbit she summon is very strong, however, herself is not. But none the less, those rabbit hits like a road roller da. Try her if you have her and SM.
Comes with heavy SP gen and neutral toolkit that counters debuff based hero, notably Lion and Shub. Definitely one of the most unique wizards.
Basically Labelle, but better. Infinite range, high DPS, res shred, 1 chain based, and only needs MR to function. Very capable choice all around.
Very solid DPS and flexible in many challenge compositions, capable of fast clear times without limited supports. Prefers Hanee in most scenarios.
A hero equipped with everything needed to make them broken in PvP, bar Eva Ignore. Who knew this kind of kit would lead to a monster in colo and arena? Certainly not me.
Resu is a very nice skill to have in various situations such as arena and ordeal, and Nightingale herself isn't bad either.
The best debuffer in the game and can give free 3 chain. Having her around is never a bad thing especially if you are to tackle contents that has high survivability pressure.
One of the most versatile buffers in PvE contents, as her consistent SP generation ability is nearly irreplacable.
A versatile support that, alongside buffs, helps provide consistent 3 chain activations and pushing, which helps with many heroes' range problems.
Terrifying buffs when ally is half health, and only sees use in competitive ordeal when this can be consistently abused. Powercreeped otherwise.
Possesses one of the best offensive utility buffs in-game, and heals a lot on top of that. Only works when the fight is mostly stationary, however.
Insane block gen with high Accu and CC buffs. Short duration makes him less useful in colo. Very fun striker in arena.
Insane damage buffs that straight up outclasses Woopa in terms of potency and consistency. The strongest buffer in game in terms of raw damage bonus.
Very good disrupt hero, comes with tank ignore, neutral damage, damage immunity and more. Does just about everything and often irreplacable in that regard.
Essential defensive buffer for heroes that want to take hits. Almost a 1:1 clone of Ferris, the second prophet of the apolocalypse.
Incredibly powerful heals capable of replacing Ferris and Gueronica when against high hit count enemies. Versatile choice in arena and ordeal.
If you do not have Halla, then he is a top priority for hero selects and such. He is just this ridiculously versatile.
A hero designed to counter to the arena meta involving insane multi tick heals. Do consider picking him if you are competitive in arena.
Despite being designed to enable Zeus, her defense buffing capability can be quite notable. It is not a bad idea to keep her at low inheritance to minimize her heals to enemies.
Schild, but priest, and that alone carves out a niche for herself. Plus, ignoring debuff immunity has some interesting applications such as being able to work in Sera.
Ridiculous block gen capability when leader has enough SP. Requires accessories to reach her full potential. Also, 15 second downtime does hurt, so clear fast.
Note (not in any specific order)
The single most essential hero for lower investment clears in challenge thanks to her ridiculous sustain capability.
Versatile Evasion tank that is a competitive choice in end game Colo and Arena. One of the top tier tanks in game. Very recommended.
High innate pen alongside incredibly fast tank ignore damage makes him ridiculous in colo and arena. Also shuts down resurrection spam via SP drain.
A genuinely threatening support in Arena due to his global stun, strong heals, and team wide SP gen. Tanking and Eva debuff should also not be taken lightly.
Good damage with threatening debuffs that cannot be cleansed, most notably buff prevention, alongside stun. An incredibly powerful and fun choice for arena.
Deal insane amount of damage against stationary bosses and is mostly neutral at that. Also provides the highest percentage team wide Resistance buff in game.
One of the most threatening DPSes in arena given her tank ignore and team wide knockback, making her a hard counter against melee heroes.
Possesses every quirk that may makes a hero viable in colo and arena, on top of good damage. Kill her fast or prepare to die.
Hits like a truck and provide many debuffs. Excellent at both being the main DPS and sub-DPS in many comps. Do note that his shred has range issue though.
Very good buffer, both offensively and defensively while providing 3 chain generation. Damage done buff is also quite universal.
Very good HA and CC buff even in late game standards. Very versatile and is a staple for beginners and veterans alike. Very recommended
Very good Armor/Resis buffer with a bit of added offensive buffs. DPS potential against multihitters should not be underestimated either. Very recommended.
Possesses good sustain and Eva ignore on certain parts of his skill. Self evasion buff and chance to block damage makes him incredibly annoying to kill.
Post-buff Leon is actually a decent choice starting out, and sometimes see use in late game arena as a high armor low hit count damage dealer
A generally capable challenge DPS that can potentially reach sub 30 second clears with Kaede. Also has the highest percentage armor shred in game.
HP scaling Armor/Resis buff makes Alex a very good tank. Does not take much investment either and can be obtained from quest. Very recommended.
Possesses a wide variety of utility alongside absolutely ridiculous block gen capability as long as she is getting hit. Can see use a variety of contents.
A capable HP tank in ordeal to counter hard hitting bosses. Often used as an alternative to Vernil.
Good damage on top of farming capablility. A team of D'art can auto almost all early to mid game stages, and will make your farming life way easier.
High burst and not block hungry at all. SP shred is a nice bonus. Recommended.
A good support all around, providing 40% CR decrease and 40% atk buffs. Works well with Carpet Bomb which also shreds 30% Armor/Resis. Recommended.
Very high damage, but damage output is affected by pretty much every single offensive stat in game. Still recommended.
While her base damage isn't particularly notable, she will demolish bosses with larger hit boxes. Range is still an issue. Currently the fastest option in C17.
A capable HP scaling DPS and is a decently low investment option in non-Inferno Total War stages. In regular contents, Rpen is still an issue.
Build him if you are struggling with the second stage of Fortress of Raging Souls. Eva ignore, dispel, and innate penetration is not something to be underestimated
A capable attack buffer with some good utilities mixed in. While she has currently not found a specific niche, her kit is sufficiently solid to see use in the future.
Incredible neutral burst with ramping damage on further 3 chains. If you can sustain her 3 chains, she will certainly be a force to be reckoned with.
A very capable DPS in standard contents. SP generation helps with her long animation time, though penetration is still an issue.
Provides fixed team wide penetration buff with SBW along with super 3c. Very recommended.
Disposable tanking object can be incredibly useful in ordeal given its capability for tanking dispel. She's not a joke anymore, and is widely used for ordeal.
Good damage with instantaneous shred scaled to his HA, but his mechanic isn't friendly for challenge delegation. Can still be viable for manual, however.
Decent damage. Has armor ignore and comes with 3 chain generation.
Damage is very high, but range is a big issue. Only really sees use when trying to burst down a beefy target, namely ordeal competitions.
Very high damage potential. However, as he needs to take a lot of hits, his team flexibility is limited. A very fun to use toy hero.
One of the hardest hitting promote hero. Can consider using, the cooldown still hurt though.
Possesses some ridiculous self buffs and results in pretty good damage output as a result. Though, animation is a bit slow, but definitely capable in challenge.
Lost her self block gen after revamp. Now just a generic block hungry DPS with decent hit count.
Possesses a good kit all around for colo and arena, but damage is just too low to be usable.
Huge team wide CC buff, and HP scaling wave helps with mobs. However, him providing nothing but CC buffs makes him less competitive in today's meta.
He has some niche use that could work, but that's about it. His SP gen isn't bad, at least...
Very good shred hero early game, can be considered as an alternative for Maria. Flat HA debuff can provide some very interesting results in ordeal.
Can give a large amount of shield and deal a decent amount of damage, not to mention her high accuracy. However, she need specific support to function.
Decent damage but has since been outclaassed by other options. Can work decently well as a 3 chain engine if enemy has a buff.
Has a very capable kit consisting of HP scaling shred and frequent dispels. However, his damage is quite lackluster in today's meta.
Niche but has good damage given sufficient amount of 3 chains. Pretty good as an end-game toy hero, but generally not recommended for progression.
Good early to mid game hero that offers good synergy with Ibelin and comes with Atk debuff.
Decent map clear capability and doesnt need penetration sigil. Needs VoS to shine, but only in arena and often locked to Halla.
Decent consistent damage, but doesn't do anything too special.
Decent anti-air hero which can be used as one-time hard counter to Almael. But long cooldown hurts him a lot.
Consistent tank ignoring damage but damage is rather lackluster as there are many better options when it comes to what he is capable of.
Very high tank ignoring damage, but crit reliant and get hard countered by damage immnunity. Can still caught people off-guard after many meta.
Still has very high damage, good knockbacks and provide true 3c for chasers. Lost her team wide HA buffs however.
75% Resis shred is the highest in game. Does not see much use outside of events, but it's best to build one just in case.
Her damage targeting is weird. Can contest with other meta challenge DPSes with broken supports, but inconsistent clear times in auto.
One of the only sources of non-contract DT debuffs. If you don't have any other choices for DT in Total War, consider using him.
Damage is decent, but insufficiently high to be of practical use anywhere. The 6 second stun can be interesting though.
HA scaling team wide penetration buff is very useful early on, but damage falls off drastically in end game contents.
Decent Ibelin abuser that also has motion speed debuffs, which can potentially be of use for bosses that doesn't have immunity to it.
Decent tank ignore hero with multihit, very useful in RSL but close to useless otherwise.
Dispels with every block, but poor damage.
Her debuffs aren't bad, but is not something that requires your opponent's immediate attention. Also hard countered by debuff immunity.
Good block gen support for a 3 chain leader and takes no investment. Granted, she doesn't provide anything other than this. Recommended for early on.
The activating condition is too strict for every part of his passive, and the payout is not worth the effort. The team wide 50% HA buff is nice, however.
Capable shield that comes with decent buff, but she can't heal.
Comes with heal block, so she at least is useful for that. Still not worth using though.
One of the worst wizards. Not recommended.
Seimei is a dispel hero that dispels with a long cooldown. Don't use him.
Debuff is workable but not needed anywhere in game as of now. Range problem makes him a strictly worse choice than other defensive healers.

The basic resource in the game. Can be used to upgrade weapons, feed bread and berries, transfer skills, buy things from popo, inlay or take out sigils, and so on.

Gold may be obtained primarily through friend honor exchanges, quests, fishing, story and challenges stages. It can also be bought in large quantities in the fishing shop, which will always be your main source of gold income. Note that farming gold outside Fishing is not recommended as they are extremely inefficient.

Side note, selling high rarity useless identified sigil in bulk can also be a decent gold income. While there is the option of saving up for a box, what you get is completely RNG, and the box itself already cost a fortune, not to mention the money you lost by not selling those sigil.

Meat should be self explanatory. It is a resource required to play story mode, challenge mode, and raid stages. Meat can be obtained from many sources, including sending honor to friends, quests, colosseum, and may be bought in large quantities from the fishing shop. If you do not have enough meat, the 30-gem meat package from the shop is not a bad deal either.

Although meat seems like an abundant resource at first, when it comes to mid to late game farming, you would begin to realize that meat isn't as plentiful as it seems. You will need meat almost everywhere, and combined with the low drop rate of sigils in challenge and raid, you will certainly need as much of it as you can.

This should also be quite obvious. Keys are used to enter dungeons stages, and sometimes, certain event dungeon stages as well.

Keys can be obtained through daily and weekly quests. They can also be bought from travelling merchant Popo. Popo from episode 6 onwards may sell 10 keys in a single slot.

Hoarding key can be considered in the following situation:
1. You need resu rings => hoard key for fergus ring event
2. You need crystals => hoard key for weekened acceleration dungeon
3. You want to have a high ranking in collection event

Colosseum tickets, as their name suggests, is used to enter colosseum. As colosseum is the only sustainable source of gems in game without paying, this resource can be very valuable when competing for higher percentage brackets.

Apart from the regenerating tickets and from daily quest, where both of which are limited, the only other source of colosseum tickets are from travelling merchant Popo. When you see the phrase "farming Popo", this is often the primary purpose.

Popo is a chance encounter limited time shop which you can find when doing any scenario or challenge stages.

She has a 1/8 chance to appear every time you complete a scenario or challenge stage, but only Popo from Deep Sea and beyond can sell ticket, and Popo from Battlefield and beyond can sell more keys per slot. Later, popo will start selling pages, and challenge popo will sometimes sell you a chest from that challenge mode, at a very reasonable price.

Note that Popo found in Forest and Desert have 4 slots, Popo found in Deep Sea and Volcano have 6 slots, and Popo from Tundra and beyond have 8 slots.

The recommended farming spots for Popo is the highest stage with the lowest meat cost in Tundra (5-8), and Battlefield (6-3). The former is preferred when tickets is prioritized for its lower meat cost, and the latter is preferred when you want more keys.

The semi-premium currency in game. Gems are primarily used to pull for heroes and to expand inventory slots. Do not use gems to reset hero promotions.

Beginners can quickly amass a large amount of it through max levelling heroes they have not maxed before, as well as through various story quests. After the beginner gem pool, the primary source of gem income is colosseum.

Honor is used primarily for promoting heroes, and is also a necessary resource for upgrading skills as well. Honor is obtained primarily from the honor dungeon. Excess honor can be be used to buy hero home decorations.

The premium currency in game. Bridget Points can be obtained through daily logins, certain events, and occasionally appears in daily limited time rewards (if you are in global server).

You can use BP to guarantee great success on weapon upgrades and skill transfers, however it is considered a poor usage of the limited currency. It is recommended to save up BPs hero selection tickets. The value of seasonal hero selection ticket is debatable.

Fish Coins can be obtained from fishing (duh), as well as fishing related events and one-time achievements.

You can trade in Fish Coins in for anything in the fishing shop. You should prioritize earning as much as these as you can. It’s a good idea to purchase the 1600 Meat, Gold, and Random Option Ticket. Do save some fish coins to buy gold in case of events such as (sc)hammer time.

Arena coins are obtained weekly from arena. The amount you get depends on your ranking. These can also be obtained from winning (20 coins) or losing (10 coins) an arena match, and does not have an acqisition limit.

Due to this nature, one may set up a script to automatically match in arena to exploit this resource but please don't let this be you.

This is a great source of battleloids, pages, fergus point, and many other resources. The 4 star contract it offer has a chance to drop contract only hero, but is not guaranteed.

It is generally best to just use them to buy champion food.

Ordeal coins are obtained after ordeal mode finishes. The amount you get is dependent on your ranking.

These are used to purchase ordeal exclusive emotes, battleloids, pages, fergus points and growth package.

This is a great way to quickly raise your champion level as you can obtain a large number of battleloids through it. The box that cost 100 coins is also a good deal for beginners and end-game players alike.

This is what a champion food looks like. There are 4/5/6 star versions, but they all looks kind of similar. The 3 star version gives 25 points, 4 star - 150 points, 5 star - 250 points, and 6 star - 500 points.

For beginners, like any other hero, you can obtain a gem from max levelling them for the first time.

Combat wise, they are completely useless, so just send them to the champion you want and be done with them.

Iron are primary farmed from world bosses and challenge. Due to the low drop rate of sigils and inheritance items, farming iron in the newest challenge is often considered to be the most effective way to obtain iron.

Iron's only use is to create and forge sould bound weapons, and you will need a great amount when doing so. On top of that, you also need SBW materials.

Randome Weapon Option Tickets are obtained from events, weekly quests, one-time achievements, and can be purchased from fishing shop every week.

They are used to reset the options of SBW, however, due to their random nature, it takes a lot of luck. It is prefered to use these on Collab hero since copies of their SBW cannot be obtained unless you gain a second copy.

Option Ticket are only given out in some events, or can be purchased in the Bridget Shop. It is, however, not a good investment.

Option ticket can be used to change one opton of your SBW to whatever you want. Due to these, they are extremely rare and is prefered to use on SBWs that only need 1 of its option changed.

By Gem Fishing Set, it refers to the Bamboo Rod and Seiren Doll / Rubber Ducky.

It is recommended for a player to first purchase the Seiren Doll from the fishing shop as soon as you can as it is unlocked at Fishing Rank 1. The earlier you buy it and use it, the faster it pays off. The items in the fishing shop are very lucrative. Auto fish overnight for passive fish coin income. It is suggested to use an emulator to avoid destroying your device's battery life.

It should be noted that the fish coin sets aren't completely outclassed when compared to gem set. From the (not very reliable) data gathered from the survey, gem sets are around 20-40% better than fish coin sets. However, it would not be very possible for you to amass 600k fish coins in a short time to immediately make use of the fish coin set, which may severely hinder your progression.

From a long term perspective, the Seiren Doll is definitely a worthy investment. It is up to you, the player, to determine whether you want to save the 99 gems in exchange for a much slower initial progression.

Note that there are zero differences, fish coin income wise, between the Rubber Ducky and Seiren Doll, as the terrain bonuses affects nothing but fish size. For fishing events, the difference is also nonexistent for it takes place in neutral water.

After buying the fishing set, the main use of gems is to purchase contracts from Bridget Shop. This is the primary way for you to obtain new heroes.

The difference between normal contracts and special contracts is that, special contracts have higher rates for the displayed heroes. Always purchase the 10x Consectutive / Special Contracts from the shop for 50 gems as these are not only cheaper than buying 10 individual contracts, but also guarantee a premium 4* hero.

It is suggested to pull a couple of 10x Consectutive / Special Contracts prior to using your Hero Selection Ticket. This may help you to determine your suggested route.

Save your gems for rate ups with heroes you want.
Don't know what you need? Check out the "Picking Heroes" section.

Once you have a stable pool of heroes for PvE and PvC purposes, it is recommended to save your gems for seasonal heroes and potential collabs.

Seasonal limited banners return at approximately the same time every year. There are currently 14 seasonal heroes in total, and they can only be obtained from their respective seasonal limited banners (or with 5000 BP). The list of seasonal heroes and their approximate schedule can be found in the Seasonal Schedule tab.

Although collab dates and contents are impossible to determine ahead of time, going by past patterns, there will usually be 2 or 3 collabs within a given year. Save your gems just in case, as collab teasers will only be shown one week prior.

Expand when you believe it is necessary, as it is a permanent upgrade and you will eventually have an use for it. It is generally useful to keep around 10-20 inventory slots, namely hero, weapon, berry, sigil, and book slots, open while farming for resources for convenience sake.

The abovementioned ways are not the only ways you can spend your gems. Rather, they are the only ways that are worth the cost. It is generally advised not to use your gems anywhere else.

Do note that buying the monthly meat pack is not a bad investment. However, the value of which depends on the player's needs, and it is best to rate its worth yourself.

Mana Essences can be obtained from primarily from LoPF, as well as from one-time achievements and through extracting rings.

Their only use is to reroll ring sub slots, however you will need a large amount when doing so.

Flame Essences can sometimes be obtained from LoPF.

These are used to increase the option of rings to its maximum amount.

Manacar Rings are obtained from Manacar World Boss.

The possible subslots for Manacar Rings are:

- Armor Penetration
- Resistance Penetration
- Damage Reduction
- Maximum HP Increase
- Attack Speed
- Accuracy
- Evasion

LoPF rings can be gained in the Legend of Primal Flames. 
The possible subslots for LoPF Rings are:

- (PvE Only) Mercenary EXP (Increases Player Level EXP)
- (PvE Only) Hero EXP (Increases EXP gain for all heroes)
- (PvE Only) Scenario Gold Increase (Increases Gold drops in Stages)
- (PvC Only) Physical Damage Increase
- (PvC Only) Magical Damage Increase
- (PvC Only) Armor Increase
- (PvC Only) Resistance Increase
- (PvC Only) %HP Increase
- (PvC Only) Critical (Chance) Resistance Increase

Although resu rings are put at a separate tab and is referred to differently, they are simply LoPF rings with the resurrection option. Obviously, the types of rings that resurrection option can appear on is not limited to the picture shown.

The resurrection sub slot is very rare, it takes player several months of farming just to obtain one if they are lucky. When you have obtained one, it is not a bad idea to use fergus points to reset conversion limit as to perfect the ring subslots.

Note that, the resurrection option can only appear on the bottom most (third) sub slot of LoPF rings. If you wish to farm for a resu ring, convert the third slot of 6* LoPF rings as doing so have the same mana essence cost as converting 5* LoPF rings, but with better subslot quality.

- Resurrect to a certain %HP when it is lowered to 0, and gain 1.5 second invincibility

Two-Dimensional Potential rings are extremely valuable items obtained from certain events. They are fixed to 2 sub options and always has a CC main stat at a 6* Manacar ring equivalent.

What sets this ring apart from regular 6* CC rings is, you can roll LS on its sub options (6% per slot, 12% max), and because this is what makes this ring unique, you will always want to roll for this specific sub option.

There are generally two cases when this ring would see use.

1. When you need more than 8.1% LS (the maximum amount to which regular LS main stat rings can provide). Events such as Don't Mess with Fergus or Hungry Hungry Fergus typically have those requirements.

2. When you need both CC and LS. FoRS Stage 3 Rael is one such example, where she has 60% CR while demanding more than 7% LS (else you die to reflect). Your damage dealers in ordeal or arena who can use the additional damage alongside survivability also fits into this criteria.

3. In PVE, as decribed later, when, due to either their own mechanics or to party composition, damage dealers gain no benefit from sub slots.
As there are 3 primary relevant contents in the game, ring recommendations can be split into the 3 sections, Colosseum, Arena, and PvE.

Subslots matter more than main options. This is because the "perfect" ring in colosseum is so incredibly rare that it does not justify throwing away one that isn't of the correct main option.
 
You cannot deal damage if you are dead. Therefore, to maximize survivability. here are some references to help you choose the optimal ring.

1. Resu ring always take priority, optimally with CR subslots.

2. DR rings > CR rings when there is no external sources of DR buff.

3. CR rings > DR rings when there are external sources of DR buff (e.g. Caeneus' 40% DR self buff).

4. CR rings >> DR rings when your opponent has high eCD (effective crit damage, in other words, CD * CC).

5. Heroes that focuses on stacking Evasion should always use Eva ring above all else.

If your damage dealer does not have any issues surviving, then rolling the 2 other subslots into magical / physical damage increase depending on your damage type (ignore this if your DPS uses neutral damage) can provide better quality of life.

For primary options, LS on damage dealers have the most impact when it comes to survivability as it is essentially a second passive, then followed by offensive options (CC, CD). Armor and Resis main stats may benefit tanks, whereas HA main stat can benefit buffers and healers that scale off of it.

COLOSSEUM ONLY RINGS ALSO WORK IN ARENA. If you didn't know, now you do.

The only difference that sets ring recommendations apart from arena to colosseum is that, resu rings does not work in arena. Therefore, the following points should be used as reference for arena from a survivability perspective:

1. CR rings > DR rings, unless the hero in question is not receiving any external DR buffs. Rare, but not impossible (e.g. resu Halla).

2. Heroes that focuses on stacking Evasion should always use Eva ring above all else.

However, arena isn't just about survivability. After all, assassinating certain threats before they murder you is also of utmost importance, seeing as these would have no counter otherwise.

This means that heroes that employ the "kill them before they kill you" strategy (often fast, bursty, tank ignore damage dealers) would prefer rings with physical / magical damage increase or Accuracy to ensure you can effectively carry out this strategy.

How does CR work and why is it preferable over DR?

Let's begin with what CR does. The defensive capability that CR provides is directly correlated to the opponent's CD and CC. To put it mathematically, the effective damage reduction (eDR) that CR provides is calculated as:

eDR = 1 - (1 + CD * (CC - CR)) / (1 + CD * CC)

With the average base CD and CC in CQ being around 145% and 45% respectively, 10% CR would make for an average of 8.8% effective reduction in damage. Of course, this value becomes more effective the more CD your opponent has.

If you are interested in how CR behaves in an eDR perspective, play around with this graph, where y = eDR, x = CC, a = CD, and b = CR. Please don't touch anything aside from the slider bars.

Although DR functions in a similar way, where the more you have the more effective it is, it is very easy to cap out DR from various sources in arena without the use of DR rings, thereby the bonuses provided will go to waste.

As arena requires every single hero to be flexible, the minor advantages that DR has in cases where DR is not capped is not worth sacrificing the versatility of using CR rings. Oh yeah and in colo, CR can appear alongside resu, so that's that.
In PvE contents, check your stat against the boss' stats, and optimize accordingly. Here are some tips to optimize your ring choices:

0. ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS consider it from your current team's context. Rings are flexible as they can be equipped and unequipped at will, so it is easy to optimize once you have built a large collection of it.

1. For damage dealers, prioritize offensive ring main options. CD and CC are preferred for more damage, and LS if you are having trouble surviving. HA is more often than not preferred on buffers, unless the buffer is for Armor / Resis buffs. However, if you do not yet have a sufficiently big collection of rings, subslots should still be of priority.

2. If you can obtain sufficient penetration, or close to enough, with rings, always prioritize getting enough penetration. If you do have enough penetration but your accuracy is insufficient to completely nullify enemy evasion, use rings to supplement your accuracy. If it is somewhere in between, then consider using a mix of the two. However, if you must choose from one, weigh your options to see which would provide the largest damage increase in a team's context.

3. If a hero reaches both the penetration and accuracy requirement (check your heroes' kit and sigils against challenge stage mechanics and stats; basic math, you're not a grade schooler), prioritize Two-Dimensional Potential rings. The additional lifesteal can be rather useful. That is unless you have hit 100% CC when accounting enemy CR, in which case you can simply run a CD ring, and sub slots does not matter in this case.

4. For buffers who are often independent from ring subslots, whatever is fine as long as they can survive. In this case, both DR ring or resu ring (one or the other) can be capable choices. That is, unless, they have some unique mechanics that uses their own stats, for instance, using their own penetration to buff allies (Haruki). Reading is important, but I'm sure that will be fine if you have gotten here.

After all that information, as a beginner, what kind of rings should you hunt for?

It is generally a good idea to prioritize obtaining a ring with some accuracy subslots to reach the challenge accuracy requirement. Math out how much you need yourself depending on what DPSes you are running.

Otherwise, beginners should prioritize hunting for resu rings as a long term objective. However, if you obtain a ring with 2 Apen / Rpen subslots or with 2 accuracy subslots, it is a good idea to reroll the slot that is not the same as the previous two to complete a ring with 3 penetration / accuracy subslots.

Once you have reached end game, these will be of incredible help in challenge and arena, as well as in events such as ordeal and Hasla War. This advice is also applicable to other ring options, where it is recommended to keep any rings you get with 3 of the same slot (or any ring with combinations of Apen / Rpen and Accuracy) as they may be of use in the future.

5* penetration rings are as good as useless end game wise, seeing as not having the maximum upgrades can immensely affect your damage output due to Armor and Resistance's hyperbolic growth; it should be rather clear if you paid attention to CQ Maths 101.

Speaking of HP... Manacar HP options are in the triple digits at max, whereas LoPF HP% options only work on training stats (no inheritance, no berry, no sigils). That sounds totally useful, am I right?

The intended way to obtain manacar rings is, well, by farming manacar. However, this is largely inefficient as your meat could be spent somewhere more useful. Still, for beginners, it is recommended to grind a couple rounds of it to obtain usable rings to supplement your main challenge carry.

If you are patient enough, you can grind LoPF indefinitely as long as you do not clear the stage. The optimal way to do this is via bringing an inherited hero along with 2 random low star heroes, with Ibelin as your champion (not necessary, but can significantly speed up the grind).

Otherwise, the most efficient way to grind rings is to wait for Sneaky Sneaky Fergus Dungeon (or as we call it, ring dungeon) which returns every 2-3 months. From there, you can obtain a large amount of ring boxes and would provide you with a better chance of obtaining something useful.

Crystals Sword Fragment are obtained from FoS. Some events can sell plenty of those, be sure to stock up on it if you can.

Old Weapons can be obtained from various sources, but the most consistent of which are daily quests and orchard bonus rewards.

These are items used for creating and forging SBW, using an old weapon as base. It cost a lot of crystal fragments to get a soul bound weapon to 6*, where they truly shine.

Orchard is the place where player can plant berry trees to get berries.

In addition, player can purchase Staff/Animals/Scarecrow to upgrade the efficiency of their orchard.

Life Essense are mainly obtained from playing scenarios. They can also be bought in the fishing shop.

Player can use Life Essense to plant berry for a prolonged period of time, which often nets better reward. While you can use them to skip the process, it is not recommended due to the ridiculous amount needed.

While Gem Set for Orchard is often considered lack luster, they do provide a significant boost to the amount of berry you obtain from them. However, that is all it offers. For player who doesn't wish to max berry all their hero, they are not a necessity.

Inheritance Pages can only inherit your units up to a particular level:

I Inheritance Pages can only inherit up to 5
II Inheritance Pages can only inherit up to 10.
III Inheritance Pages can only inherit up to 15.
IV Inheritance Pages can only inherit up to 20.
V Inheritance Pages can only inherit up to 25.

Inheritance Books can inherit at any level. In general, Page Is are for i1-5, Page IIs for i6-10, Page IIIs, for i11-15, Page IVs, for i16-20,  Page Vs, for i21-25, and books to inherit any higher.

These items are obtained through farming challenge mode, quests, fishing shop, as well as during certain events. Obviously, books have a much lower drop rate while pages are more common. Sometimes, if you encounter a King Goblin in scenario and kill him, he can drop a book upon death.

Alchemy can be used to combine several pages into its higher level counterpart. 

Note that, during alchemy events, they often give out incredibly efficient formulas for the player, so it is recommended to save until then.

Refer to the Definitely Original Tier List for recommended SBW options for every hero.

Upgrading weapons costs a LOT of gold when you are hunting for the desired option, and is generally your main expenditure of gold. You can upgrade your SBWs at any star level as the upgrade cost and the pool of options are the same regardless.

Save your gold or fish coins until Hammer Time, where the increased great chance can save you quite a bit of resources; your personal sanity included.

To prior to inlaying sigils, you must use another SBW to punch a hole in the SBW you want to slot a sigil in. It does not have to be an identical SBW. Afterwards, you can put a sigil in the SBW. When you inlay a SBW that already has a slot, it does not destroy the sigil present on the SBW.

However, it is significantly harder to acquire double inlays (2 sigil slots). The second slot can only be unlocked by supplying extra materials, unlocking at 100 points.

4* SBW gives 5 points
5* SBW givess 10 points
6* SBW gives 20 points
A single fergus point gives 10 points

Resource wise, given how abundant old weapons are, supplying 20 4* SBWs is the cheapest way to obtain a second sigil slot. In comparison, using 5 6* SBWs will cost 50% more crystals, as well as 75% more iron and gold.

Fergus Points are used to guarantee double inlay on a SBW. They are consistently obtained in the stage March of Darkness in FoRS. They can also be obtained from daily logins, one-time achievements, and sometimes, events as well.

Fergus Points can also be used to achieve great upgrades, as well as to reset ring conversion limit. However, only do so if you have a lot of excess FPs, as these are still rare resources.

For beginners, the sigils obtainable from fishing shop is incredibly useful.

Given that you can obtain the highest rarity of unidentified sigils here, it is highly recommended for new players to purchase these during early and midgame.

Set sigils are dropped from world bosses, and when inlayed alongside the sigil it associates with, it gives some additional stats. Due to this nature, they are late game items. However, you can sometimes obtain the required sigil from daily logins.

1.t: Same buff does not stack, even if you use a copy of the same hero.

3.t: Buffs that increases the respective stat by a fixed amount.

Hero V has a 1250 HA buff that stacks 5 times in total. If V has 2000 base HA, she will have a total of 
2000 +  1250 * 5 = 6450 HA when she reaches max stacks.
Buffs that multiplies the respective stat by a fixed amount.

Hero Yuna and Orfeo has a 50% HA buff. If the hero receving buff has 2000 HA, it will have 
2000 * (1 + 0.5) * (1 + 0.5) = 4500 HA post buff.
All Additive buffs are calculated before the Multiplcative buffs, the order of when buff is applied does not matter.
[ (Base) + ∑ (Additive Buff) ] * ∏ [1 + Multiplicative Buff] = Post Buff Stat
Hero Caeneus has 800 Addtive Armor/Resistance Buff and a 30% multiplicative Armor/Resistance Buff. If Caeneus has 1200 Res, it will have [ 1200 + 800 ] * [ 1 + 0.3 ] = 2600 Res.
DR however, the calculation is completely different.
[ 1 - [ 1 - Base DR ] * ∏ [ 1 - DR buff ] ] = Post Buff DR
Hero Caeneus has a 40% DR buff. If Caeneus has 40% base DR, He will have [1 - (1 - 40%) * (1 - 40%)] = 64% DR.
Buff amplification is a multiplicative effect that affects each buff individually. Note that some buffs cannot be affected by buff amplification.
[ [Base] + ∑ [Additive Buff * (1 + Amplification)] ] * ∏ [1 + Multiplicative Buff * (1 + Amplification)] = Post Buff Stat
Using the aforementioned scenario of Yuna and Orfeo buffing a hero with 2000 HA, when Aubrey is used, the hero will have 2000 * [1 + 0.5 * (1 + 0.25)] * [1 + 0.5 * (1 + 0.25)] = 5821.25 HA post buff.

1.t: eDamage = Damage Multiplier * HA * eCD * Chance to Hit * ( 1 - DR ) * { 1 / [ 1 + 0.0034 * (Defense - Penetration ) ] }

3.t:
It is important to understand first what is the base value to which buffs are based on. A simple way to tell what a hero's base stat is, is what is shown on the hero stat screen.

When the term "base stat" is referred anywhere else, it means the stats shown here. This is applicable to every single stat, with the exception of Attack Apeed (AS).
All HP, CC, CD, AS, Accu, and Eva buff are additive.
HA, Armor, Resis, Apen, and Rpen buffs are either Additive or Multiplicative. This can be distinguished by the % sign.
Armor and Resistance affects physical and magical damage respectively, and are used to reduce the damage you take via this reciprocal formula:
Every 294 Armor / Resis change the physical / magical damage you receive to 1/2, then 1/3, 1/4, and so on.

Apen/Rpen is subtracted from the enemy Armor/Resis during damage calculation.
Neutral damage ignores both Armor and Resis.
In this formula, {Arm/Res - Apen/Rpen} cannot be lowered to below 0. So having too much Penetration does nothing.

All attacks that have a source have at least a 5% chance to hit and 5% chance to miss no matter what. 
However, there are exceptions to this rule. 
The attack in question may not have a source, thereby it cannot miss. 
The attack may act as a delete button, setting your HP to 0 no matter what
The attack may simply be bugged.
This can be negative.
[Result is always at least 5% or at most 95%]

CC is the chance to crit and CD is the additional % of damage you will do when crit.

CR on the other hand, decreases the chance of enemy's chance to crit you.

The effective critical damage is calculated by this formula:
You cannot go to negative CC.

Attack Speed is an indicator of how many autoattacks a given hero can perform per second.

A hero's base AS is dictated by the weapon they are wielding. This value is given as a decimal, and is defaulted as 1 if no weapon is equipped. Equipment AS consists of weapon upgrade and ring sub options, and is multiplicative to base. However, AS buffs behave differently and is additive to the product of equipment and base AS as well as one another.
AS = Base AS  * (1 + Equipment AS) + AS buffs

Attack Speed Cap: 250%, or 2.5 autoattacks per second
Damage Reduction Cap: 80%
When damage is done, the number will be displayed.
When the damage is gray, it means that the damage dealt is less than 50% of the effective damage. This can be caused by not having enough penetration, or the enemy having more than 50% DR.

When the damage is yellow, it means that the opposite. Damage dealt is more than 50% of the effective damage. However, having yellow number doesn't automatically mean that you have sufficient penetration.
When the damage is red, it means the damage is a critical hit, and thus will deal more damage based on your critical damage stat.
When the number is white, it means the damage is dealt to the enemy shield.
All damage colors shown above have their outlines and fills inversed.

However, if you obtain a ring with 2 Apen / Rpen subslots or with 2 accuracy subslots, it is a good idea to reroll the slot that is not the same as the previous two to complete a ring with 3 penetration / accuracy subslots.

Once you have reached end game, these will be of incredible help in challenge and arena, as well as in events such as ordeal and Hasla War. This advice is also applicable to other ring options, where it is recommended to keep any rings you get with 2 or more of the same slots (or any ring with combinations of Apen / Rpen and Accuracy) as they may be of use in the future. You can eventually reroll the last line into a 3 line ring you want.

This is especially applicable to DR, where you will need 12, yes 12, 3 line 6* DR rings for stable Total War clears.

5* penetration rings are as good as useless end game wise, seeing as not having the maximum upgrades can immensely affect your damage output due to Armor and Resistance's hyperbolic growth; it should be rather clear if you paid attention to CQ Maths 101.

Speaking of HP... Manacar HP options are in the triple digits at max, whereas LoPF HP% options only work on training stats (no inheritance, no berry, no sigils). That sounds totally useful, am I right?

The intended way to obtain manacar rings is, well, by farming manacar. However, this is largely inefficient as your meat could be spent somewhere more useful. Still, for beginners, it is recommended to grind a couple rounds of it to obtain usable rings to supplement your main challenge carry.

If you are patient enough, you can grind LoPF indefinitely as long as you do not clear the stage. The optimal way to do this is via bringing an inherited hero along with 2 random low star heroes, with Ibelin as your champion (not necessary, but can significantly speed up the grind).

Otherwise, the most efficient way to grind rings is to wait for Sneaky Sneaky Fergus Dungeon (or as we call it, ring dungeon) which returns every 2-3 months. From there, you can obtain a large amount of ring boxes and would provide you with a better chance of obtaining something useful.
